    9.3 Others
    Indian Steel Processing Centres are governed by a robust regulatory framework of labour laws, taxation, and environmental
    laws. Taxation has become much more organised with the rollout of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), which has reduced
    the tax incidence to a uniform GST rate on steel products, with 12% on domestic use items such as iron and steel household
    articles and 18% on articles such as railway tracks and pipes). Further, India is planning to impose a border adjustment tax
    on steel imports to put the domestic producers on an equal footing. The tax would cover various charges that are not included
    under GST, i.e., cess and state charges, which form approximately 12% of the price of steel available for sale in India.
    Indian labour laws have been merged into four principal codes to ease compliance and enhance workers' welfare. They are
    the Code on Wages, the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, the Code on Social Security, and the
    Industrial Relations Code. The reforms seek to universalise minimum wages, make timely payment, and give emphasis to
    occupational safety, thus fostering a good work environment and promoting economic growth.


    Environmental laws for Steel Processing Centres are strict, and the operations are sustainable. The Environment Protection
    Act, 1986, and other rules and regulations control pollution and environmental protection). Initiatives by the government,
    such as the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and the Corporate Responsibility for Environmental
    Protection (CREP) have also encouraged industries to implement cleaner technologies and minimise their impact on the
    environment. Recent policies also encourage decarbonization in the steel sector via improvements in energy efficiency and
    renewable energy use.

    9.   Key Threats and Challenges to the Indian Steel Industry

•        Raw Material Price Volatility: The Indian steel industry is highly dependent on raw materials such as iron ore, coking
         coal, and scrap. Price fluctuations in these inputs significantly impact production costs and market competitiveness.
         While India benefits from abundant iron ore reserves, domestic price volatility arises from factors like mining
         regulations and environmental concerns. The steel sector’s heavy reliance on imported coking coal, which constitutes
         a significant portion of steel production costs, further exposes it to global price fluctuations and supply disruptions,
         adding instability to the industry’s pricing structure. The price and availability of steel coils are subject to volatility
         and supply constraints arising from various external factors beyond the Company’s control, including global and

                                                                    228
    domestic demand-supply dynamics, logistics and processing costs, inflation, governmental regulations and policies,
    overall economic conditions, production levels, market competition, duties and taxes, trade restrictions, transportation
    costs and currency exchange rate fluctuations.

•    Logistics Costs: Logistics remains a major bottleneck for India’s steel industry, with transportation inefficiencies
     inflating costs. Steel production and its raw materials require bulk transportation, yet India’s infrastructure lags behind
     global standards. With a high percentage of steel plants located inland, the cost of rail and road freight is elevated,
     leading to significant cost disadvantages compared to global competitors. Indian steel producers are estimated to
     incur logistics costs of 15-17% of revenue, far exceeding the global average and impacting India’s competitiveness
     in both domestic and international markets.

•    Dependency on Imports for Certain Grades of Steel: Despite being a major steel producer, India remains
     significantly reliant on imports of high-quality coking coal, as domestic availability of low-ash coking coal is limited
     relative to the requirements of the steel industry. The Ministry of Steel notes that most domestically produced coking
     coal has high ash content, resulting in substantial imports to meet steel-sector requirements. India also continues to
     rely on imports for certain high-grade and specialised steel products, particularly where domestic availability or
     capacity remains insufficient. This import dependence exposes steel producers to international commodity-price
     movements, exchange-rate fluctuations and potential supply-chain disruptions. In the case of coking coal, the
     dependence is particularly significant because it is a major component of steel manufacturing costs, thereby affecting
     the industry's cost competitiveness and reducing raw-material self-sufficiency.

10. Use of Automation, AI, and Digital Tracking for Efficiency and Optimisation
The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), automation, and digital tracking technologies holds transformative potential
for the Indian steel industry, addressing several critical challenges. These technologies improve efficiency, reduce waste,
and optimise distribution, driving competitiveness and sustainability.

AI and Predictive Analytics can forecast raw material prices with high accuracy, enabling steelmakers to time procurement
and hedge against price volatility. Additionally, AI-driven inventory management allows for better demand forecasting and
optimised stockpiles, reducing excess inventories. For instance, Tata Steel has used AI to cut excess inventories.
Additionally, Tata Steel has developed an in-house AI model, NIRN-AI, to forecast the coking-coal price index over a
three-month horizon, providing inputs for sourcing strategy and procurement decisions. AI can also identify alternative
sourcing options, reducing reliance on volatile imports like coking coal.

Automation enhances production processes by employing robotics and automated guided vehicles (AGVs), increasing
throughput and reducing labour costs. Automated material handling systems and port automation can reduce turnaround
times, cutting logistics costs. AI systems also optimise production schedules, improving capacity utilisation.

Digital Tracking and IoT enable real-time monitoring of raw material shipments, improving supply chain transparency
and reducing delays. AI-powered route optimisation and smart logistics platforms further enhance distribution efficiency
by minimising idle time and freight costs. These innovations could reduce logistics expenses, aiding in meeting the National
Logistics Policy's cost-reduction targets.

Together, these technologies can reduce production costs, improve energy efficiency, and meet stringent environmental
standards, positioning India’s steel industry as a leader in both efficiency and sustainability. With significant investments
and government support, these advancements could help the sector meet its 255 MT production goal by 2030-31.

11.3 Competitive Benchmarking

Bombay Coated & Special Steel Limited (BCSSL), incorporated in 2019, emerged as one of the steel processing centres in
India, specialising in transforming Steel Coils into high-quality Processed Steel Products. Their expertise encompasses
slitting, cut-to-length, shearing, and embossing, enabling the delivery of processed steel products tailored to meet exact
customer needs. They serve a wide range of industries through OEMs and ODMs, with applications in home and
commercial appliances (such as air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, and water heaters), as well as general
engineering sectors including cleanrooms, electrical components, ventilation systems, automotive parts, and more.




                                                           233
For the Home & Commercial Appliances sector, the company processes coated and hot-rolled steel coils into products used
in air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, water heaters, and more. For the General Engineering sector, the
company specialise in processing non-coated and galvanised plain coils into blanks, supporting the manufacture of
automobiles, pharmaceutical cleanrooms, electrical components, and air ventilation systems.

BCSSL, being a Steel Processing Centre (“SPC”), plays a crucial role in India's steel supply chain by acting as
intermediaries between steel producers and end-users. Beyond precision processing, slitting, cut-to-length, shearing, and
embossing, SPCs add value by managing inventory and enabling just-in-time delivery. This ensures businesses across both
urban and remote regions receive processed steel products in a timely and cost-efficient manner.

Since 2021, the Company has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited and/or its holding
company (“JSWCPL”), pursuant to an agreement for the regular supply of steel coils. They procure steel coils from
JSWCPL as well as other suppliers and process them using advanced engineering techniques and high-precision machinery
to manufacture Processed Steel Products. Their long-standing and strong supplier relationships ensure stability and
reliability in sourcing, enabling us to efficiently and consistently meet customer requirements. The Company also carries
out embossing for colour-coated sheets, which is required for refrigerator panels.

The Company’s customer-centric approach enables it to provide tailored solutions that align with both functional and
aesthetic expectations, and just-in-time deliveries of Processed Steel Products align with the requirements of their
customers. Their customers majorly include OEMs and ODMs like Haier Appliances India Private Limited, IFB
Refrigeration Limited, Dixon Electro Manufacturing Private Limited, Amber Enterprises India Limited, Western
Refrigeration Private Limited, PG Technoplast Private Limited, EPack Durable Limited, Kruger Ventilation Industries
(India) Private Limited, Elegant Coatings Private Limited, Magnum MI Steel Private Limited and A. K. Engineering. These
customers span multiple industries, including consumer durables and home appliances, electrical equipment and
components, automotive and auto components, HVAC and refrigeration, electronics and electrical manufacturing services,
industrial engineering and capital goods, steel processing and metal fabrication, infrastructure and construction-related
industries, renewable energy and power equipment, FMCG and packaging, as well as general manufacturing and industrial
trading enterprises. Such diversification of their customer base across industries reduces our dependence on any single
customer or industry segment.

The company operates in four strategically located facilities across India, serving both the Home & Commercial Appliances
and General Engineering sectors.

• Western Region (Maharashtra & Gujarat): Their facilities at Wada (Palghar) and Bhiwandi (Thane) are well-
  connected through the Mumbai–Ahmedabad and Mumbai–Nashik highways. Their proximity to major industrial hubs,
  Pune, Nashik, Vasai-Virar, Boisar, Umbergaon, Khopoli, Silvasa, Aurangabad, and Vadodara, enables efficient material
  flow, quick turnaround times, and cost-effective logistics.

• Northern Region (Rajasthan): The Ghiloth facility, located on the Delhi–Jaipur Highway (NH8) about 90 km from
  Delhi International Airport, caters to OEMs and ODMs across Gurgaon, Noida, Bhiwadi, Manesar, Jhajjar, Rudrapur,
  and Dehradun, ensuring timely supply and reduced transit costs.

• Southern Region (Andhra Pradesh): Their Sri City facility, situated within one of South India’s advanced industrial
  corridors along NH16, benefits from its presence in a multiproduct SEZ with DTZ, FTWZ, and an electronics cluster.
  Located around 100 km from Chennai Airport, it serves appliance manufacturers in Chennai, Gummidipoondi, and
  Sriperumbudur, offering just-in-time delivery while also supporting the General Engineering sector.

The company has demonstrated robust financial performance, with a 20.00% y-o-y growth in FY26 and a 29.51% CAGR
during FY24-FY26, outpacing its industry peers. While BCSSL’s EBITDA, EBIT, and PAT margins moderated in FY26
after improving in FY25, they recovered in Q1FY27, reflecting improved operating performance and profitability.
Additionally, the company has effectively reduced its gearing ratio from 4.31x in FY24 to 2.78x in FY26 and 2.00x in
Q1FY27, signalling a reduction in financial leverage. ROCE remained above the peer median in FY26 at 16.40%, despite
moderating from FY25. These metrics highlight BCSSL’s improving financial position and ability to generate returns,
while order volumes for air conditioners, home refrigeration, and commercial refrigeration are typically lower during June
to September.

12.4 Definitions



                                                          237
Blanks                     Blanks are the output of the process, which involves cutting Slit Coils or Embossed Slit
                           Coils into the desired length based on customer specifications.
Steel Coils                Steel Coils shall include Coated Steel Coils and Non-Coated Steel Coils.
Coated Steel Coils         Coated Steel Coils shall include galvalume steel coils, colour-coated steel coils and
                           galvanised steel coils.
Non-Coated Steel Coils     Non-Coated Steel Coils shall include both cold-rolled steel coils and hot-rolled steel coils.
Processed Steel Products   Processed Steel Products shall include Slit Coils, Embossed Slit Coils, Blanks, Embossed
                           Blanks and Sheared Blanks.
Slit Coils                 Slit Coils are the output of the process, which involves the slitting of Steel Coils into
                           narrower widths based on customer specifications.
Embossed Slit Coils        Embossed Slit Coils are the output of the process, which involves slitting of embossed
                           colour-coated steel coils into the desired width based on customer specifications.
Embossed Blanks            Embossed Blanks are the output of the process, which involves cutting Embossed Slit
                           Coils into the desired length based on customer specifications.
Sheared Blanks             Sheared Blanks are the output of the process, which involves cutting Blanks into the
                           desired length, width or both based on customer specifications.

Overview

We are a steel processing centre engaged in the business of converting steel coils into value-added processed steel products.
Our core competencies include precision slitting, cut-to-length processing, shearing, and embossing of steel coils into slit
coils, embossed slit coils, blanks, embossed blanks and sheared blanks (collectively referred to as “Processed Steel
Products”). We cater to a diversified customer base comprising Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and Original
Design Manufacturers (ODMs).

Our Company, being a Steel Processing Centre (“SPC”), operate as an intermediary between primary steel producers and
end-users by providing value-added processing services. For the home and commercial appliances sector, we process coated
steel coils and hot-rolled steel coils into Processed Steel Products used in the manufacture of various appliances. For the
general engineering sector, we undertake specialized processing of non-coated and galvanised plain coils into blanks, used
in automotive manufacturing, pharmaceutical cleanroom infrastructure, electrical equipment, and ventilation systems. In
addition to manufacturing Processed Steel Products, we also perform logistics and inventory management functions. By
maintaining adequate inventory levels and offering just-in-time delivery solutions, we ensure timely and efficient supply
of processed steel products to customers across urban as well as remote locations, thereby enhancing supply chain efficiency
and cost optimization. (Source: CareEdge Report)

One of the Promoters of our Company, Mr. Vijaykumar Himatrai Gupta, commenced operations in 1983 as a steel trader
under the sole proprietorship M/s. Bombay Steels. In 2012, the business expanded into steel processing with the
establishment of the Bhiwandi facility, followed by the execution of a service partnership agreement with JSW Steel Coated
Products Limited (“JSWSCPL”) in 2018. Subsequently, on January 29, 2021, our Company entered into a Business
Transfer Agreement to acquire the running business of M/s. Bombay Steels on a going-concern basis. This acquisition
consolidated over four decades of trading and processing experience into the operations of our Company. Thereafter, our
Company has entered into a phase of rapid expansion and added steel processing facilities across key manufacturing regions

                                                            239
of India. We expanded our operations by establishing new manufacturing facilities in the West, North and South of India.
Our steel processing facilities are strategically located across key industrial regions in India, enabling us to serve a wide
spectrum of industries with efficiency and just in time deliveries. For further details see ‘Our Business – Manufacturing
Facilities’ on page 261.

Since 2021, our Company has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited and/or its holding
Company (“JSWSCPL”), pursuant to an agreement for the regular supply of steel coils. We procure steel coils from
JSWSCPL as well as other suppliers and process them using advanced engineering techniques and high-precision
machinery to manufacture Processed Steel Products. Our long-standing and strong supplier relationships ensure stability
and reliability in sourcing, enabling us to efficiently and consistently meet customer requirements. (Source: CareEdge
Report)

We are a multi-location steel processing centre with manufacturing facilities located at Wada and Bhiwandi in Maharashtra,
Ghiloth in Rajasthan, and Sri City in Andhra Pradesh. Our facilities are equipped with steel processing infrastructure,
including slitting lines, cut-to-length lines, shearing lines, and embossing lines, designed to achieve operational precision
and efficiency. These manufacturing facilities are spread across four strategically located sites in India, aggregating a total
area of 42,209 square meters, and are ISO 9001:2015 certified for the processing, marketing, and supply of Processed Steel
Products. Further, our Ghiloth facility in Rajasthan and Sri City in facility Andhra Pradesh has been recognized as a GEM-
4 certified green facility.

The locations of our manufacturing facilities have been selected with reference to proximity to customer delivery points.
Certain facilities are located near the manufacturing locations of customers such as Western Refrigeration Private Limited,
Amber Enterprises India Limited, PG Technoplast Private Limited, EPack Durable Limited, Kruger Ventilation Industries
(India) Private Limited, among others. This proximity enables reduction in logistics time and transportation costs, facilitates
operational efficiencies, and supports timely fulfilment of customer requirements. In addition, the clustering of certain
facilities within the same state allows for inter-facility movement of materials, thereby reducing freight time and costs as
components undergo sequential processing.

We operate with an aggregate installed processing capacity of 1,23,153 MTPA, computed on a quarterly basis for Fiscal
2027, across slitting, cut-to-length, shearing and embossing operations, as of June 30, 2026. Our installed capacity has
increased at a compound annual growth rate (“CAGR”) of approximately 23.83% between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026,
reflecting our continued focus on capacity expansion and operational scalability. For further details see ‘Our Business –
Installed Capacity and Capacity Utilization’ on page 261. Further, our long-standing authorised partnership with JSW Steel
Coated Products Limited since 2021 provides us with reliable access to quality raw materials and supports our ability to
service a diversified customer base, positioning us well for sustained growth in the steel processing industry.

We have established long-standing relationships with a diverse set of customers. Our focus on quality, value proposition,
timely delivery of our products and the price competitiveness of our offerings has enabled us to maintain long-term
relationships with our customers. In Fiscal Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, as well as for the three months period ended June
30, 2026, we served 178, 261, 252 and 225 and customers, respectively. These customers span multiple industries, including
consumer durables and home appliances, electrical equipment and components, automotive and auto components, HVAC
and refrigeration, electronics and electrical manufacturing services, industrial engineering and capital goods, steel
processing and metal fabrication, infrastructure, renewable energy and power equipment, FMCG and packaging, as well as
general manufacturing and industrial trading enterprises. Such diversification of our customer base across industries reduces
our dependence on any single customer or industry segment. (Source: CareEdge Report)

Our customer-centric approach enables us to provide tailored solutions that align with both functional and aesthetic
expectations, and just in time deliveries of Processed Steel Products aligns with the requirements of our customers. Our
customer base includes several OEMs and ODMs operating in India, including Haier Appliances India Private Limited IFB
Refrigeration Limited, Dixon Electro Manufacturing Private Limited, Amber Enterprises India Limited, Western
Refrigeration Private Limited, PG Technoplast Private Limited, EPack Durable Limited Kruger Ventilation Industries
(India) Private Limited, Elegant Coatings Private Limited and Magnum MI Steel Private Limited.

Our Promoters, Board of Directors, and senior management have been instrumental in the growth of our business and have
enabled us to capitalize on market opportunities and better serve our customers, with collective experience spanning
operations, business development, and customer relationship management. Our Promoter and Chairman-cum-Whole-Time
Director, Mr. Vijaykumar Himatrai Gupta, has over 40 years of experience in the steel industry and provides guidance in
formulating our long-term business strategies and business development initiatives, having played a pivotal role in steering
the growth and development of our Company. Our Promoter and Managing Director, Mr. Nitin Vijaykumar Gupta, has
approximately 20 years of experience in the steel industry and is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations of
the Company, as well as providing guidance on strategy formulation, business development, and customer relationships.
Our workforce is a critical asset to our operations and comprised 160 permanent employees and 4 retainership employees

                                                             240
as of June 30, 2026, who form the backbone of our business by driving innovation, ensuring quality, and maintaining the
standards expected by our customers.

Our Market Opportunity

As per the CareEdge Report, there exists a substantial market opportunity for our Company, which can be clearly
demonstrated from the following:

Role of Steel Processing Centres:

Steel Processing Centres (“SPCs”) in India are witnessing significant growth, driven by rising steel consumption across
diverse end-use sectors such as automotive, construction, infrastructure and manufacturing. As India continues to accelerate
its industrialisation and infrastructure development, SPCs are emerging as a critical link between large-scale steel producers
and end-users, providing essential services including steel slitting, cut-to-length, blanking, splitting, inventory management,
and timely distribution. These services enable industries to access steel in the precise forms and quantities required, thereby
improving efficiency, reducing waste, and optimising supply chains.

The growing demand for steel arising from infrastructure development, supported by government initiatives and
urbanisation, has contributed to the increasing relevance of SPCs. In parallel, expansion in the automotive and
manufacturing sectors has resulted in greater demand for processed steel products that meet specific technical and
dimensional requirements. By customising steel products and reducing dependence on in-house processing by end-users,
SPCs support improved manufacturing efficiency, reduced material wastage and optimised supply chains. The increasing
adoption of just-in-time (“JIT”) delivery models, particularly in the automotive and consumer durables sectors, has further
reinforced the importance of SPCs in ensuring timely availability of processed steel inputs.

Growth of Key Service Segments:

•   Cut to Length: The market size of Cut to Length service type grew at a CAGR of 8.3% from CY20 to CY25, reaching
    a market size of USD 1,707 million by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.8% from CY26 to CY30
    reaching a market size of USD 2,337 million by CY30.

•   Slitting: The market size of Slitting service type grew at a CAGR of 8.7% from CY20 to CY25, reaching a market
    size of USD 1,501 million by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.2% from CY26 to CY30 reaching
    a market size of USD 2,095 million by CY30.

•   Blanking: The market size of the Blanking service type grew at a CAGR of 8.7% from CY20 to CY25 reaching a
    market size of USD 892 million by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.4% from CY26 to CY30
    reaching market size of USD 1,250 million by CY30.

•   Splitting: The market size of Splitting service type grew at a CAGR of 8.8% from CY20 to CY25 reaching a market
    size of USD 379 million by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 7.4% from CY26 to CY30 reaching
    market size of USD 531 million by CY30.

•   Others: The market size of Other service types including shearing, embossing, and surface treatment such as pickling
    and oiling, galvanizing, nickel plating, chrome plating, phosphating, etc. grew at a CAGR of 6.4% from CY20 to CY25
    reaching a market size of USD 344 million by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 5.0% from CY26 to
    CY30 reaching market size of USD 433 million by CY30.

The steady growth across all service segments highlights the increasing importance of SPCs in supporting India’s industrial
ecosystem.

Key Drivers of Opportunity:

•   Growing Demand from Construction and Automotive Industries: The construction and automotive sectors are
    major consumers of steel, driving the demand for Steel Processing Centres. Steel is critical for applications such as
    structural framing in construction and car components in automotive production. As both industries expand, the need
    for Steel Processing Centres to supply customised steel products, with reduced lead times and processing, continues to
    rise.

•   Technological Advancements in Steelmaking: Technological innovations are reshaping the steel industry, enabling
    more efficient steel production and processing. These advancements lead to lower production costs, making steel more


                                                             241
           accessible for various industries. The development of new equipment and steelmaking processes is also enhancing the
           productivity of Steel Processing Centres, enabling them to serve their customers more efficiently and cost-effectively.

•          Increased Utilisation of Steel Across Multiple Sectors: Steel’s versatility has driven its increased use in various
           sectors, including biotechnology, energy, shipbuilding, and manufacturing. Its role in heavy industries, construction,
           and machinery is expanding as demand for robust, temperature-resistant materials rises. Steel Processing Centres are
           essential for supplying specialised steel products, contributing to their growing market presence.

•          Globalisation and Competitive Market Expansion: Globalisation has opened new opportunities for Steel Processing
           Centres to cater to international markets. As the global demand for steel rises, centres are increasingly competing for
           customers worldwide. This global reach encourages service centres to improve operational efficiency, adopt advanced
           technologies, and offer better services at competitive prices, ultimately benefiting customers.

•          Rise of Local Manufacturing and Industrialisation: The shift toward local manufacturing, combined with rapid
           industrialisation, has boosted the demand for Steel Processing Centres. The establishment of new centres in emerging
           markets allows them to cater to local manufacturing needs. Additionally, the growing preference for steel in industries
           such as mining, construction, and chemicals further drives the demand for Steel Processing Centre services.

•          Expansion of India's Consumer Electronics and Appliances Sector Driving Steel Demand: The consumer
           electronics and appliances sector in India is witnessing significant expansion, fuelled by rising incomes, technological
           innovation, and growing domestic demand. As the country positions itself as a major player in the global market for
           products like smartphones, white goods, and air conditioners, the need for high-quality materials, particularly steel,
           continues to rise. Steel plays a crucial role in the production of key components such as frames and internal structures,
           which are integral to the manufacturing of these consumer products. This increased demand for durable, reliable
           materials supports the broader industrial landscape.

Notes:
   1)   Revenue from operation means revenue from operating activities
   2)   PBT means Profit before taxes expense
   3)   PAT represents total net profit after tax for the year.
   4)   EBIT means Earnings before interest and taxes expense, arrived at by obtaining the profit before tax for the year and adding
        back finance costs.
   5)   EBIT Margin is calculated as EBIT as a percentage of revenue from operations.
   6)   Adjusted EBITDA means Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation expense, arrived at by obtaining the
        profit before tax for the year and adding back finance costs and depreciation and amortisation expenses and adjusted by other
        income
   7)   Adjusted EBITDA Margin is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of revenue from operations.
   8)   PBT Margin is calculated as PBT as a percentage of revenue from operations.
   9)   PAT Margin is calculated as PAT as a percentage of revenue from operations.
   10) Return on Equity (ROE) is calculated as PAT divided by average of net worth;
   11) Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) is calculated as EBIT divided by capital employed where (i) EBIT means Earnings before
        interest and taxes expense, arrived at by obtaining the profit before tax for the year and adding back finance costs and (ii)
        Capital employed means Net worth + Total debt + Deferred tax liability;
   12) Return on Assets (ROA) is calculated as PAT divided by average of total assets;
   13) Debt to Equity Ratio is defined as total debt divided by total equity. Total debt is the sum of total non-current & current
        borrowings; total equity means sum of equity share capital and other equity;
   14) Debt Service Coverage Ratio is calculated as earning before interest and tax expenses as divided by finance cost and principal
        repayments.
   15) Fixed Asset Turnover Ratio is defined as revenue from operations divided by total of property, plant & equipment. Figures for
        property, plant & equipment do not include capital work-in-progress and Right-of-Use Assets.
   16) Current Ratio is calculated by dividing total current assets by total current liability.
   17) Net Working Capital Days refers to average working capital divided by revenue from operations and multiplied by 365 days.
        For the three-month period ended June 30, 2026, the calculation has been made by considering 91 days.
   18) Property, plant and equipment means total property, plant and equipment in assets of the company.
    19) Number of manufacturing facilities strategically located across India, enabling us to cater efficiently to a diverse customer
        base.
    20) Represents the maximum production capability of our manufacturing facilities under ideal operating conditions.
    21) Refers to the actual output achieved by our facilities during the given period.
    22) Indicates the extent to which the installed capacity has been utilized, reflecting operational efficiency.

Our Strengths

a) Established relationship with JSWSCPL Steel for supply of Steel Coils.

Our Company has been an authorised service partner of JSW Steel Coated Products Limited and/or its holding Company
(“JSWSCPL”) since 2021. Pursuant to this arrangement, JSWSCPL supplies steel coils, including galvanised plain,
colour-coated and galvalume coils, which are used as raw material in our manufacturing operations. These steel coils are
processed at our facilities through slitting, cut-to-length, shearing and embossing operations using precision machinery and
technology. Such processing activities constitute a core component of our business operations. JSWSCPL also provides

                                                                243
technical assistance to ensure compliance with prescribed product specifications and performance requirements during the
processing of blanks and sheets. Further, quality control procedures jointly established with JSWSCPL and aligned with its
benchmarks are implemented across our operations to ensure consistency, traceability and adherence to applicable industry
standards.

In addition to JSWSCPL, we have sourcing arrangements with other steel suppliers. Collectively, these arrangements enable
regular procurement of steel coils, access to technical inputs and consistency in input quality. Customers with specific
requirements for coated steel products are serviced under the authorised service partner arrangement, under which steel
coils procured from JSWSCPL are processed at our manufacturing facilities using high-precision equipment.

Our authorised service partner relationship with JSWSCPL contributes to our business engagement with original equipment
manufacturers (“OEMs”) and original design manufacturers (“ODMs”) operating in the Home and Commercial Appliances
sector and other segments of the General Engineering sector, particularly where customised processing of JSWSCPL-
manufactured steel coils is required. The arrangement facilitates continuity in raw material sourcing and supports the
efficient execution of processing activities.

c)   Strategically Located Manufacturing Network Enabling Just-in-Time Supply and Cost-Efficient Operations

We operate as a multi-location steel processing centre with manufacturing facilities located at Wada, Bhiwandi, Ghiloth
and Sri City Facility in India. Our manufacturing facilities are strategically located in proximity to major OEM and ODM
manufacturing hubs across Western, Northern and Southern India, including in close proximity to the manufacturing
locations of certain key customers such as Western Refrigeration Private Limited, Amber Enterprises India Limited, PG
Technoplast Private Limited, EPack Durable Limited and Kruger Ventilation Industries (India) Private Limited, among
others. This proximity enables efficient logistics, just-in-time deliveries and regional servicing capabilities, while reducing
transit time and freight costs. Our geographically distributed manufacturing footprint provides operational flexibility and
supports cost-efficient and timely supply of processed steel products across India.

Logistics and inventory management are integral to our operations. Each of our manufacturing facilities has dedicated
storage infrastructure for bulk storage of steel coils and processed steel products, enabling efficient material handling and
continuity of operations. We deliver processed steel products in accordance with customer specifications, including required
form and quantities, thereby supporting uninterrupted production schedules of our OEM and ODM customers.

Our inventory management practices, including maintenance of buffer stocks and steady production planning, enable us to
mitigate supply-chain disruptions and reduce the impact of volatility in steel availability, thereby supporting consistent
supply to customers.




Western India

Maharashtra, which primarily cater to customers in the Home & Commercial Appliances and General Engineering sectors

d) Integrated and Advanced Steel Processing Infrastructure

We have established an integrated and advanced steel processing infrastructure comprising high-precision slitting, cut-to-
length, shearing and embossing lines. Our machinery and equipment have been procured from a mix of reputed domestic
manufacturers and international suppliers based in South Korea, Turkiye and China. All our manufacturing facilities are
ISO 9001:2015 certified, reflecting standardized processes and consistent quality control.

As on June 30, 2026, our slitting lines have an installed capacity of 1,23,153 MTPA and are capable of processing steel
coils into slit coils with widths ranging from 22 mm to 1,850 mm and thicknesses from 0.25 mm to 3.20 mm. Our cut-to-
length lines have an installed capacity of 50,481MTPA and can process steel coils into blanks with widths ranging from
150 mm to 1,320 mm and thicknesses from 0.25 mm to 5.50 mm. In addition, our shearing lines, with an installed capacity
of 1,467 MTPA, enable precise straight edge cutting for downstream fabrication requirements, while our embossing lines,
with an installed capacity of 11,700 MTPA, allow us to deliver uniform textured and patterned surfaces enhancing
functional and aesthetic attributes.

This integrated processing capability enables us to manufacture and supply a wide range of ready-to-use Processed Steel
Products tailored to customer-specific technical, dimensional and surface finish requirements, strengthening our position
as a reliable processing partner for OEMs and ODMs in the Home & Commercial Appliances and General Engineering
sectors.

e)   High Entry Barriers Driven by Authorised Supplier Arrangements, Capital Intensity and Customer Approvals

The industry is characterised by relatively high entry barriers arising from substantial capital investments in specialised
processing equipment, inventory holding requirements, customer qualification processes and technical approval standards.
(Source: CareEdge Report)

We are engaged in the processing of coated steel coils and hot rolled steel coils into slit coils and blanks/sheets for the
Home and Commercial Appliances sector, including air conditioners, home and commercial refrigeration, washing
machines and water heaters. We also process non-coated steel coils and galvanised plain coils into blanks/sheets for the
General Engineering sector, including applications in automobiles, pharmaceutical clean rooms, electrical components and
air ventilation systems.

Our customers, including OEMs and ODMs, require processed steel products conforming to precise technical specifications
linked to their end-use applications. For example, refrigerator outer panels require scratch-free surfaces with uniform
embossed patterns, while components used in air conditioners require tight dimensional tolerances and consistent surface
finishes to ensure compatibility with downstream coating and fabrication processes. Compliance with such specifications
necessitates specialised plant and machinery and skilled manpower, which involve significant investment and technical


                                                           248
capability. Steel processing facilities are generally required to be located in close proximity to customer manufacturing
units to support just-in-time deliveries. Serving customers across multiple regions requires the establishment of multiple
processing centres, involving substantial capital expenditure in land, buildings, plant and machinery. In addition, we
maintain adequate inventory across our manufacturing facilities to address short-term fluctuations in customer demand
arising from seasonality and market volatility.

Vendor onboarding by OEMs and ODMs involves detailed technical evaluations, quality audits and validation processes,
conducted directly or through appointed technical consultants. Our manufacturing facilities are subject to periodic audits to
ensure compliance with customer-specified quality standards and applicable regulatory requirements. Successful
completion of these processes is required for empanelment and continuation as an approved vendor. OEMs and ODMs
depend on reliable, high-precision and just-in-time supply of processed steel products, which positions steel processing
centres as an essential intermediary between primary steel producers and end-use manufacturers. Steel producers generally
focus on large-scale steel coil manufacturing, while downstream processing involves customer-specific requirements,
proximity to customer locations, specialised infrastructure and skilled labour.

Our operations are supported by authorised supplier relationships, audited manufacturing facilities, established customer
relationships and demonstrated capability to meet stringent technical and quality specifications in a capital-intensive
operating environment.

We are led by qualified and experienced Promoters and senior management team, who possess the expertise and vision to
manage and grow our business. Our Company is promoted by seasoned entrepreneurs with experience of four 4 (four)
decades in steel trading, processing and downstream supply chain operations. Our Promoters bring deep industry
knowledge, long-standing customer and supplier relationships, and a proven track record in the steel trading and processing
industry. Our Promoters, Vijaykumar Himatrai Gupta, Nitin Vijaykumar Gupta and Bhawna Nitin Gupta are well versed
with steel industry practices and have been instrumental in our Company’s growth and development. Our Promoter,
Vijaykumar Himatrai Gupta has more than 4 decades of experience in steel trading and processing business along with

Our Promoters are supported by a professional management team comprising of Senior Management Personnel and Key
Managerial Personnel with strong operational, technical, and financial expertise, enable us to understand and anticipate
market trends, manage our business operations, growth and leverage customer. We believe that the knowledge and

a competitive advantage, as we seek to expand our steel processing capacities and, as well as expansion in our existing
markets and new markets. For further information, see “Our Management- Board of Directors” and “Our Promoters and

Our Strategies

The strategies described below have been approved by way of a board resolution passed by our Board of Directors at their
meeting held on September 24, 2026.

a) Strategy to Expand Customer Base and Diversify End-User Industries

We intend to expand our customer base and increase our market share across the industries we serve by diversifying our
end-user segments and strengthening our presence in non-seasonal product categories. As of June 30, 2026, approximately
89.93% of our Processed Steel Products were supplied for the manufacturing of home and commercial appliances, including
air conditioners, home refrigeration, and commercial refrigeration products, while the remaining 10.07% were supplied for
the manufacturing of water heaters, washing machines, and products in the General Engineering sector.

Demand for air conditioners, home refrigeration, and commercial refrigeration products is typically subject to seasonality,
with relatively lower order volumes observed during the period from June to September. (Source: CareEdge Report) In
order to mitigate the impact of such seasonality and demand fluctuations, we propose to increase supplies of our Processed
Steel Products to OEMs and ODMs engaged in the manufacturing of water heaters, washing machines, and products in the
General Engineering sector. Our strategy includes strengthening relationships with existing customers, onboarding new
customers, and expanding our product portfolio, supported by consistent product quality and reliable service delivery.

We believe that increasing supplies to applications such as water heaters, washing machines, and General Engineering
products will enable us to diversify our end-user base and reduce dependence on OEMs and ODMs manufacturing air
conditioners, home refrigeration, and commercial refrigeration products. This diversification is expected to reduce


                                                            249
concentration risk, mitigate the impact of cyclicality and seasonality associated with certain appliance segments, and allow
us to leverage demand growth across a broader range of end-use industries.

According to the CareEdge Report, the market size for air conditioners in India is projected to grow at a CAGR of 15.00%,
reaching ₹ 936.1 billion by CY29. Further, as per the CareEdge Report, the water heater market in India is projected to
grow at a CAGR of 11.3%, reaching ₹350.1 billion by CY29. We believe this growth trends present opportunities to expand
supplies across multiple appliance categories.

India represents a potential growth opportunity for the Company’s diversification into automotive and auto ancillary
applications. India is the third-largest automobile market globally and is the largest manufacturer of two-wheelers, three-
wheelers, and tractors, and is among the top 5 manufacturers of passenger and commercial vehicles. The Indian auto
ancillary market was valued at ₹6,730 billion in FY25 and is projected to grow to ₹10,178 billion by FY29, at a CAGR of
approximately 10.90% during FY25 to FY29. The Company believes that this growth in the automotive ecosystem may
provide opportunities to expand the application of its Processed Steel Products in automotive and auto ancillary
components, which typically exhibit relatively stable demand patterns. (Source: CareEdge Report).

Through the implementation of this strategy, the Company aims to improve capacity utilization, broaden its customer
portfolio, and generate incremental revenue streams. Increased diversification across end-user industries is expected to
support operating leverage, reduce reliance on seasonal appliance segments, and enhance business resilience over the long
term.

b) Expansion of our existing Ghiloth Facility to capitalize on industry opportunities.

Our Manufacturing Facilities spread across four (4) locations in the country and have an aggregate total area of 42,209 sq.
mts. Over the years, we have strategically expanded and enhanced our manufacturing capabilities and continue to do so to
meet market demands. For further information, see “-Our Strengths - Strategically Located Manufacturing Network
Enabling Just-in-Time Supply and Cost-Efficient Operations” on page 246.

Our Ghiloth Facility is situated on land admeasuring 11,250 square meters at Plot No. SP7-356, RIICO Industrial Area,
Ghiloth, District Alwar, Rajasthan, India. As of June 30, 2026, computed on a quarterly basis for Fiscal 2027, the facility
is equipped with two (2) slitting lines with an aggregate installed capacity of 36,000 MTPA, three (3) cut-to-length lines
with an aggregate installed capacity of 26,400MTPA, and one (1) shearing line with an installed capacity of 6,300 MTPA.

Our Company has observed higher utilization of its overall installed capacity during the second half of the financial year
as compared to the full-year average. In order to address this trend and support incremental demand during peak operating
periods, we plan to expand the Ghiloth Facility by installing one (1) additional cut-to-length line. In connection with the
proposed expansion, our Company has acquired an additional parcel of land admeasuring 11,250 sq. mtrs. at Plot No. SP7-
355, RIICO Industrial Area, Ghiloth, District Alwar, Rajasthan, India, adjoining the existing facility. The said land was
acquired by the Company pursuant to sale deed dated September 29, 2025, for a total consideration of ₹116.87 million,
which has been funded through internal accruals and/or borrowings.

Our aggregate installed steel processing capacity increased from 301,541 MTPA in Fiscal 2024 to 350,411 MTPA in Fiscal
2025, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 48,870 MTPA, or approximately 16.21%. Further, our aggregate installed
capacity increased from 350,411 MTPA in Fiscal 2025 to 4,62,411 MTPA in Fiscal 2026, representing a year-on-year
increase of 1,12,000 MTPA, or approximately 31.96%. Overall, our installed capacity increased by 1,60,870 MTPA
between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026, representing a cumulative increase of approximately 53.30%. Accordingly, our
installed capacity registered a compound annual growth rate ("CAGR") of approximately 23.83% during this period,
primarily on account of incremental capacity additions across our slitting, cut-to-length, embossing and shearing processing
lines. For further details, see “Our Business – Installed Capacity and Capacity Utilization” on page 261.

As per the CareEdge report, the global Steel Processing Centre (“SPC”) industry grew at a CAGR of 8.6% from CY20 to
CY25 reaching a market size of USD 8.2 billion by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 8.6% from CY26
to CY30, reaching a market size of USD 12.4 billion by CY30. Growth in the global SPC industry is driven by demand
from steel-consuming end-user industries such as construction, automotive, infrastructure, and industrial manufacturing,
supported by urbanisation, infrastructure development, and adoption of advanced processing technologies.

The CareEdge report also highlights growth across key geographic regions. The Asia Pacific region (excluding India)
recorded at a CAGR of 6.5% from CY20 to CY25 reaching a market size of USD 104.5 billion by CY25. It is further
projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.5% from CY26 to CY30 reaching a market size of USD 143.1 billion by CY30. Europe
grew at a CAGR of 6.1% from CY20 to CY25, reaching a market size of USD 56.5 billion by CY25. It is further projected
to grow at a CAGR of 6.1% from CY26 to CY30 reaching a market size of USD 75.7 billion by CY30. North America
grew at a CAGR of 5.6% from CY20 to CY25 reaching a market size of USD 34.9 billion by CY25. It is further projected
to grow at a CAGR of 5.4% from CY26 to CY30, reaching a market size of USD 45.6 billion by CY30. The Middle East
and Africa region grew at a CAGR of 4.9% from CY20 to CY25 reaching a market size of USD 6.3 billion by CY25. It is
further projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.9% from CY26 to CY30 reaching a market size of USD 8.0 billion by CY30.

As per the CareEdge report, the Indian SPC industry grew at a CAGR of 8.6% from CY20 to CY25 reaching a market size
of USD 8.2 billion by CY25. It is further projected to grow at a CAGR of 8.6% from CY26 to CY30, reaching a market
size of USD 12.4 billion by CY30, supported by demand from automotive, infrastructure, engineering, and manufacturing
sectors, as well as government-led infrastructure initiatives. (Source: CareEdge Report)

We intend to leverage these industry trends by expanding our presence in international markets and increasing exports,
while continuing to strengthen our domestic operations. Our established steel processing facilities, operational procedures,
quality control systems, and ability to supply customised, value-added steel products enable us to service customers across
multiple locations and end-user industries. We also seek to leverage our long-standing customer relationships to supply
products to additional locations of existing customers within India and overseas.

Our strategy to increase exports will enable us to diversify our revenue base. Furthermore, expanding our geographical
footprint will help us mitigate the risks associated with economic fluctuations in any one region. We also believe that there
exist significant opportunities to cross-sell our products and offer the same products to additional locations of our existing
customers, leveraging our long-standing relationships with them and existing manufacturing capabilities.

e)   Continue to reduce operational costs and improve operational efficiencies

                                                              252
We intend to enhance our profitability and strengthen our competitive position by continuing to focus on disciplined cost
management and improving operational efficiencies across our steel processing operations. Our strategy is centred on the
following key initiatives:

    •    Scale Efficiency: We seek to benefit from economies of scale by expanding and optimising our processing
         capacities. Our steel processing operations involve certain fixed overheads, including utilities, employee costs and
         depreciation of assets. Improved capacity utilisation is expected to reduce fixed costs per unit, thereby enhancing
         operating leverage and improving overall profitability. As volumes increase, our cost structure will become more
         efficient, enabling us to deliver improved margins.

    •    Yield Optimisation and Throughput Efficiency: We continuously refine our steel processing cycles and production
         planning processes to improve material yield and minimise processing losses. By enhancing throughput efficiency
         and optimising production scheduling, we aim to maximise output from existing capacities and improve overall
         operational performance.

    •    Lean Inventory Management and Logistics Support: As part of our steel processing services, we also facilitate
         logistics and inventory-related functions for our customers. We typically maintain inventory equivalent to
         approximately one to one and a half months of customer requirements and offer just-in-time delivery solutions.
         This approach enables efficient inventory turnover, reduces handling inefficiencies and ensures timely delivery of
         processed steel products to our customers.

    •    Reduction in Steel Processing Costs through Automation and Asset Ownership: We continue to focus on reducing
         steel processing costs by increasing automation across our operations and enhancing plant throughput. Automation
         initiatives are expected to reduce manual intervention, improve process consistency and lower operating costs over
         the long term.

In line with this objective, our Company proposes to utilise a portion of the Net Proceeds from the Issue towards the
acquisition of certain capital equipment currently held under lease arrangements with Siemens Financial Services Private
Limited (“Siemens”). These capital equipment items are deployed at our Ghiloth Facility and are integral to our business
operations. The proposed acquisition of these assets is expected to result in cost savings through the reduction of lease-
related expenses, improved asset utilisation and greater operational control, thereby contributing to enhanced operational
efficiency and margin improvement. For further details, see “Objects of the Issue” on page 117.

Our Business Operations

We process steel coils into value-added Processed Steel Products, including Slit Coils, Blanks/Sheets, Embossed Slit Coils,
Embossed Blanks and Sheared Blanks, strictly based on customer specifications. These products are primarily used in home
and commercial appliances and general engineering applications.

A. Slitting:

In the slitting process, Steel Coils are slit into narrower widths in accordance with customer specifications to produce Slit
Coils. Where customers require Slit Coils as the final product, the process concludes at this stage, and the Slit Coils are



                                                            253
packed and dispatched. In other cases, the Slit Coils are transferred to the subsequent processing stage, such as embossing
or cut-to-length, as applicable.

Our slitting operations deliver high dimensional accuracy and are designed to meet precise customer requirements. The
advanced slitting process ensures optimal material utilization without introducing surface defects, thereby minimizing waste
and enhancing overall cost-effectiveness.

         Raw
                       Planning for      Preparation        Machine            Slitting     Post Slitting    Packaging &
       material
                         Slitting        for Slitting        Setup            Operation      Inspection        Dispatch
       Handling


Explanation of the Slitting process is as under:

 1.   Raw Material Handling

 The slitting process begins with the receipt of Steel Coils in accordance with
 specific customer specifications. Upon arrival, the Steel Coils are inspected
 and verified to ensure compliance with the prescribed quality standards.
 Once verified, the Steel Coils are scheduled for slitting as per the processing
 plan aligned with customer requirements.



 2.   Planning for Slitting

 Prior to the commencement of slitting operations, a detailed planning sheet
 is prepared, incorporating all relevant technical details and processing
 requirements. This planning sheet serves as a reference for the machine
 operator and is handed over to ensure accurate execution. Proper planning
 at this stage is critical to maintaining consistency and minimizing
 processing errors.

 3.   Preparation for Slitting

 At this stage, the operator verifies the Steel Coil number, dimensions
 (including size and weight), and grade against the planning sheet to ensure
 accuracy. The Steel Coil is then unwrapped, and its dimensions are
 measured using calibrated instruments to maintain precision. All relevant
 data is recorded, and the Steel Coil is prepared for processing.



 4.   Machine Setup

 In this stage, input data is entered into the system in accordance with the
 slitting plan and machine parameters. The Steel Coil is transferred to the
 uncoiler using a coil car, threaded through the pinch rolls, passed through
 the slitter head, and subsequently through the leveler. Proper machine setup
 is essential to achieve accurate and consistent slitting.




                                                             254
 5.   Slitting Operation

 Before commencing full-scale production, sampling and testing are
 conducted to verify that the setup meets the required quality standards. If
 the sample does not meet the prescribed specifications, the Steel Coil is
 reprocessed through the slitting machine. Upon successful sample approval,
 regular slitting operations commence, with continuous quality monitoring
 to ensure consistency throughout the process.



 6.   Post-Slitting Inspection

 Upon completion of the slitting process, final sampling and quality
 inspection are carried out. If the Slit Coils do not meet the required
 standards, they are segregated and kept under quality observation for further
 evaluation or rework. Slit Coils that pass the inspection are cleared for the
 next stage of processing or for dispatch, as applicable.




 7.   Packaging & Dispatch

 Where no further processing is required, the Slit Coils are weighed for
 weight verification and packaged in accordance with company standards.
 The packaged Slit Coils are then transferred to the Finished Goods (FG)
 storage area and dispatched in line with the company’s logistics
 arrangements and customer delivery schedules. In cases where further
 processing is required, the Slit Coils are transferred to the subsequent
 processing stage, such as Embossing or Cut-to-Length, as applicable.



B. Embossing

In Embossing, based on customer specifications, certain slit colour coated steel coils undergo an embossing process to
achieve decorative or functional surface finishes. In this process, the slit coils are passed through embossing rollers to create
raised or recessed patterns, resulting in Embossed Slit Coils. Where Embossed Slit Coils are required as the final product,
they are packed and dispatched accordingly. In other cases, the Embossed Slit Coils are further processed through the cut-
to-length stage.

The embossing process enhances surface characteristics such as rigidity, slip resistance, and visual appeal, and is undertaken
in accordance with customer requirements. This process is particularly relevant for applications such as refrigerator panels,
where patterned surfaces improve structural strength and aesthetics.

         Raw                              Preparation                                              Post             Final
                        Planning for                         Machine          Sampling &
       material                               for                                               Processing        Handling &
                        Embossing                             Setup             Testing
       Handling                           Embossing                                             Inspection         Dispatch



 1.   Raw Material Handling

 The embossing process begins with the receipt of slit colour-coated steel
 coils in accordance with customer specifications. Upon receipt, the slit
 colour-coated steel coils are inspected for identity, surface quality, and
 overall condition. Following verification, the coils are scheduled for
 embossing in line with the approved processing plan.




                                                              255
2.   Planning for Embossing

A detailed planning sheet is prepared, outlining key information such as
specifications, dimensions, and embossing requirements. This planning
sheet is handed over to the designated machine operator to guide the
machine setup and embossing operations. Proper planning at this stage
ensures precision, consistency, and adherence to customer requirements.




3.   Preparation for Embossing

At this stage, the operator identifies the assigned slit colour-coated steel coil
and cross-verifies its coil number, dimensions (size and weight), and grade
against the planning sheet. The coil is then unwrapped, and its dimensions
are physically verified using calibrated measuring instruments. All
observations are recorded in a logbook to ensure traceability and quality
assurance.


4.   Machine Setup

In this stage, input data is entered into the machine’s control system in
accordance with the planning sheet and equipment parameters. The slit
colour-coated steel coil is transported to the uncoiler using a coil car,
threaded through the pinch rolls, and guided into the embossing rolls to
initiate the embossing process.




5.   Sampling and Testing

Before commencing full-scale embossing, trial samples are taken and tested
to verify conformity with the prescribed quality standards. If the samples do
not meet the required specifications, necessary adjustments are made to the
machine settings and sampling is repeated. Once the samples are approved,
embossing operations commence, with continuous monitoring of product
quality throughout the process.



6.   Post-Processing Inspection

Upon completion of the embossing process, final sampling and quality
inspection are carried out. If the results are not satisfactory, the embossed
slit coils are segregated and kept under quality observation for further
evaluation or rework. Embossed slit coils that pass the inspection are cleared
for the next stage of processing or for dispatch, as applicable.




                                                              256
 7.   Final Handling and Dispatch

 Where no further processing is required, the embossed slit coils are weighed
 for weight verification, packaged in accordance with company standards,
 and transferred to the Finished Goods (FG) storage area. The embossed slit
 coils are subsequently dispatched or transferred as per the Company’s
 logistics arrangements and customer delivery schedules.

 In cases where further processing is required, the embossed slit coils are
 transferred to the next processing stage, i.e., Cut-to-Length, as applicable.


C. Cut-To-Length Process (CTL)

In the cut-to-length process, Slit Coils or Embossed Slit Coils are precision-levelled and cut into sheets or blanks of
specified lengths, resulting in Blanks or Embossed Blanks. Where customers require Blanks or Embossed Blanks as the
final product, the process concludes at this stage, following which the products are packed and dispatched. In other cases,
the Blanks are forwarded to the subsequent processing stage, namely shearing.

The cut-to-length process ensures accurate levelling and dimensional precision in accordance with customer specifications.
The resulting Blanks or Embossed Blanks are customised to meet specific end-use requirements and are particularly suited
for applications where tight dimensional tolerances are critical for downstream manufacturing.

         Raw                                                                     Post                          Final
                       Planning for      Preparation         Machine                        Sampling &
       material                                                               Processing                     Handling &
                           CTL            for CTL             Setup                           Testing
       Handling                                                               Inspection                      Dispatch


 1.   Raw Material Handling

 The Cut-to-Length (CTL) process begins with the receipt of Slit Coils or
 Embossed Slit Coils in accordance with customer specifications. Each batch
 of Slit Coils or Embossed Slit Coils is carefully inspected to verify identity,
 quality, suitability, and compliance with customer requirements. Upon
 verification, the material is scheduled for CTL processing as per the
 approved processing plan.




 2.   Planning for CTL

 A detailed planning sheet is prepared, capturing all operational, technical,
 and quality specifications required for the CTL process. This planning sheet
 is handed over to the designated machine operator to guide machine setup
 and operations. Proper planning at this stage ensures smooth processing and
 adherence to customer specifications.




                                                             257
3.   Preparation for CTL

At this stage, the operator identifies the assigned Slit Coil or Embossed Slit
Coil and cross-verifies its coil number, dimensions (size and weight), and
grade against the planning sheet. The coil is then unwrapped, and its
dimensions are physically verified using calibrated measuring instruments
to ensure accuracy. All observations are recorded in a logbook to ensure
traceability and quality assurance.




4.   Machine Setup

In this stage, input data is entered into the machine’s control system in
accordance with the planning sheet and equipment parameters. Using a coil
car, the Slit Coil or Embossed Slit Coil is transported to the uncoiler,
threaded through the pinch rolls, and guided through the leveler to prepare
the material for precise length cutting.




5.   Sampling and Testing

Before full-scale processing begins, trial samples are taken and tested before
starting CTL. If the sample does not meet the required standards,
adjustments are made to the machine settings, and sampling is repeated.
Once the sample passes quality checks, the processing begins, and the
operator continues to monitor product quality throughout the process.




6.   Post-Processing Inspection

Upon completion of the CTL process, final sampling and quality inspection
are conducted. If the results are not satisfactory, the Blanks or Embossed
Blanks are segregated and kept under quality observation for further
evaluation or rework. Blanks or Embossed Blanks that pass the inspection
are cleared for the next stage of processing or for dispatch, as applicable.




                                                           258
 7.   Final Handling and Dispatch

 a) Blanks: Where no further processing is required, the Blanks are weighed
    for weight verification, packaged in accordance with company standards,
    and transferred to the Finished Goods (FG) storage area. The Blanks are
    subsequently dispatched or transferred as per the Company’s logistics
    arrangements and customer delivery schedules. In cases where further
    processing is required, the Blanks are transferred to the next processing
    stage, i.e., Shearing.

 b) Embossed Blanks: The Embossed Blanks are weighed for weight
    verification, packaged in accordance with company standards, and
    transferred to the Finished Goods (FG) storage area and subsequently
    dispatched or transferred as per the Company’s logistics arrangements
    and customer delivery schedules.

D. Shearing

In the shearing process, Blanks received from the cut-to-length stage are resized by length, width, or both, resulting in
Sheared Blanks. Upon completion, the Sheared Blanks are packed and dispatched to customers.

The shearing process enables precise resizing of Blanks to meet customer-specific dimensional requirements. The resulting
Sheared Blanks, produced in standardised or customised sizes, are well suited for direct use in customers’ downstream
manufacturing processes.

                                                          Machine          Sampling
      material            for              for                                            processing        Handling

 1.   Raw Material Handling

 The shearing process begins with the receipt of Blanks. Each batch of
 Blanks is carefully inspected to verify identity, dimensions, physical
 condition, and compliance with customer requirements. Upon successful
 verification, the Blanks are scheduled for shearing in accordance with the
 approved processing plan.



 2.   Planning for Shearing

 A detailed planning sheet is prepared, capturing the required material
 dimensions, specifications, and operational parameters for the shearing
 process. This planning sheet is handed over to the designated machine
 operator to guide the setup and execution of the shearing operations.




                                                           259
3.   Preparation for Shearing

At this stage, the operator identifies the assigned Blanks and cross-verifies
the batch number, dimensions (size and weight), and grade against the
planning sheet. The Blanks are then unwrapped, and their dimensions are
physically verified using calibrated measuring instruments to ensure
accuracy. All observations are recorded in a logbook to ensure traceability
and quality assurance.




4.   Machine Setup

In this stage, input data is entered into the shearing machine’s control system
in accordance with the planning sheet and equipment parameters. The
Blanks are then manually fed into the shearing machine for cutting into the
desired lengths or widths.




5.   Sampling and Testing

Before commencing full-scale shearing operations, trial samples are
produced and tested to verify conformity with the prescribed quality
standards. If the samples do not meet the required specifications, necessary
adjustments are made to the machine settings and sampling is repeated.
Once the samples are approved, shearing operations commence, with
continuous monitoring of product quality throughout the process.




6.   Post-Processing Inspection

Upon completion of the shearing process, final sampling and quality
inspection are conducted. If the results are not satisfactory, the Sheared
Blanks are segregated and kept under quality observation for further
evaluation or rework. Sheared Blanks that pass the inspection are cleared
for dispatch.




7.   Post-Processing Inspection

In the final stage, the Sheared Blanks are weighed for weight verification,
packaged in accordance with company standards, and transferred to the
Finished Goods (FG) storage area. The Sheared Blanks are subsequently
dispatched or transferred as per the Company’s logistics arrangements and
customer delivery schedules.

Further, each of these processing operations - Slitting, Cut-to-length, Embossing and Shearing can function either
independently or as part of an integrated processing sequence, depending on the specific requirements and specifications
of our customer. For instance, Steel Coils initially processed through a slitting line may subsequently undergo embossing
and/or cut-to-length process before final dispatch, or in some cases, may be supplied directly to the customer as Slit Coils.
As a result, these operations are interconnected and often overlap, with one process frequently feeding into or
complementing another within the processing cycle.

Customers

Our customer engagements are dependent on our ability to consistently deliver high-quality Processed Steel Products that
meet the stringent precision requirements of OEMs and ODMs operating in the Home & Commercial Appliances and
General Engineering sectors. We focus on understanding customer specifications and delivering customized Processed
Steel Products, including requirements relating to dimensions, shapes, and embossing, based on the intended end-use by
the ultimate consumer. As on June 30, 2026, we supplied our Processed Steel Products to 178 customers. Our products are
transported to customers on either a cost, insurance and freight (CIF) basis or a free on board (FOB) basis, depending on
the agreed commercial terms.

The customer onboarding process typically spans three (3) to six (6) months and involves initial engagement through market
research, inbound enquiries, or participation in industry events, followed by customer audits of our manufacturing facilities
to assess our technical capabilities. Onboarding is completed only after successful negotiations on commercial terms.

Our customer base includes leading OEMs and ODMs such as Haier Appliances India Private Limited, IFB Refrigeration
Limited, Dixon Electro Manufacturing Private Limited, Amber Enterprises India Limited, Western Refrigeration Private
Limited, PG Technoplast Private Limited, EPack Durable Limited, Kruger Ventilation Industries (India) Private Limited,
Elegant Coatings Private Limited, Magnum MI Steel Private Limited, and A. K. Engineering. We have established long-
standing customer relationships through consistent quality, customized product offerings, and responsive customer service.
